info.title: @@APP_NAME@@ — Gateway
info.description:
The Tabularia API: everything the interface does goes through it.

**Sign in** with an API token in the header `Authorization: Bearer tab_…` (Settings → API tokens, or a service account under Administration). Read-only tokens refuse every request that changes something.

**Stable** for integrations: `auth/me`, `projects`, `flows`, `flows/{id}/run-now`, `runs`, `datasources`, `datasources/{id}/refresh`, `tasks/export`, `lineage`, and the webhooks. The rest may change between minor versions. The guide, with recipes and webhook signature checks, is docs/api.md in the repository.

post.description:
Opens a session. The token comes back in the body, for the scripts and APIs that put
it in the `Authorization` header, and in an `HttpOnly` cookie for the browser, which
so never keeps it where JavaScript reads it.

get.description:
Whether the sign-in page must ask for the first administrator: only on a stack
that allows it (AUTH__FIRST_RUN_SETUP, never in production) and while no account exists.

post.description:
Creates the first administrator and signs it in. Possible once: from the moment any
account exists this answers 409, and on a stack without first-run setup 404.

The sample-data container's sign-in: the start-up token from SECURITY__KEYS_DIR, for
a session as the first administrator. 409 until that administrator exists (the
container waits for it); 404 on a stack without first-run setup or token.

Closes the session the request comes with: from here its token no longer holds,
wherever it was copied.

get.description:
Where one is connected now: a browser, another computer, a script. The observer only
their own (see `_shared`).

schema.title: Response My Sessions Auth Sessions Get

delete.description:
Closes one of one's own sessions. The others' are not seen: 404. The observer closes
only the one they ask from, that is they sign out.

post.description:
«Sign out of the other devices»: only this one stays open. Not for the observer (see
`_shared`).

get.description: Public (pre-login): tells the frontend whether to show the SSO button.

Starts the authorization code flow: generates state/nonce/PKCE, puts them in a signed,
short-lived cookie and sends the user to the IdP.

Return from the IdP: validates, provisions, synchronizes the groups and opens an
INTERNAL session (the same as the local login's).

put.description:
The language chosen in the interface. The interface sends it at sign-in and
when it changes; the emails the product sends this user speak it.

get.description:
The rule of a new password (core/passwords.py), for the interface to check
a form before sending it: the same numbers and list the gateway applies.

schema.title: Response Password Rules Users Password Rules Get

post.description:
One's own password, from the settings menu. The current password is asked
again (whoever finds a session open does not get the account for good); the
rules are those of user creation. As when an administrator sets it, the
other sessions and the API tokens close; this one stays.

delete.description:
Deletes the user. Their CONTENT stays (the data belongs to the organization, not to
the person): flows/datasources/connections/runs lose only the reference to the owner.
The personal permissions, the group memberships and the ownership of uploads not in a
flow yet disappear with them.

The AUDIT instead is not touched: it is append-only and must stay readable after the
person has gone, otherwise deleting an account would delete the evidence of what they
did. Only the `actor_id` reference is reset, while `actor_label` keeps the email of
then — exactly the reason that field exists (see models/audit.py).

schema.title: Response My Tokens Auth Tokens Get

post.description: A token for one's own scripts: it holds with one's own permissions, never more.

delete.description:
Revokes one of one's own tokens (the one asking too, when it is read-write: a script
may withdraw its credential when the work is done; a read-only one changes nothing,
not even this). The others': 404.

get.description:
All the valid tokens, with who owns them: to withdraw the one that leaked. To the
observer without who and from where.

422 says which and why, with a code the panel translates), then they are saved: what

post.description:
«Test connection»: the engine tries the external ClickHouse with these values, step by
step, and saves nothing. Administrators only: it makes the engine open a connection
to the address given.

put.description:
Changes the ones given, all or none: a 422 says which and why, with a code the
panel translates. Saved, they apply at once in this process, within
`REREAD_EVERY` seconds in the others (the rollout ones: when they start again).

post.description:
Kubernetes: the orchestrator restarts their pods one at a time. Docker Compose, or
Kubernetes without the chart's right: the administrator says they restarted them.

delete.description: Stops a rollout: the pods already restarted stay, the others keep the old value.

put.description:
Sets the autoscaling bounds of a kind of worker: first on the cluster, then
saved (what one reads here is what the cluster has).

delete.description:
Stops keeping the panel's bounds: the cluster keeps the current ones until the
next deployment of the chart puts its own back.

put.description:
Changes what is given. Turning on wants address and token; the first time the
forwarding starts from now (the history stays in the Audit panel). Off and on again it
picks up where it left off: no gaps.

post.description:
Sends a test event to Splunk now (it does not go through the queue) and says what it
answered: token, index, certificate and network are checked here.
«Back up now»: the first orchestrator that looks (every few seconds) makes it.

Writes, reads and deletes a probe object with the key, from the engine (the
workers write there the same way), and says whether the key can list the bucket.

A new version from the same language version and packages as the latest: after
a failed build, or to start again from an updated base image.

Runs go back (or forward) to a version already built: its image is still in
the registry.

patch.description:
Description and, above all, the two flags: ADMIN (from then on every member of the
group is an administrator, and stops being one by leaving it) and OBSERVER (every
member reads the panels without being able to write in them). They are independent: an
admin group does not need the second, because whoever administers reads already.

get.description: All the banners, newest to oldest.

PUBLIC, without authentication, and that is the point: the notice is read BEFORE
signing in. Saying it only to whoever is in already would mean informing someone after
taking their data.

It exposes nothing not meant to be read by anyone: it is a text the organization
publishes on purpose.
All the known engines, with their state and how many flows still use them.

get.description:
The conversations of WHOEVER ASKS, newest first. Never those of others.

For an OBSERVER the list is empty by construction — their conversations are not
saved — but it is said out loud here: if one day something wrote a chat in their
name, it would not be served to anyone signing in with the shared account anyway.

A whole conversation, ready to put back on screen: questions, answers, steps and the
cost of each turn.

Downloads the COMPLETE result of an assistant query.

The chat shows at most `AI__MAX_RESULT_ROWS` rows; the file holds them all, because
the engine runs the query again on the normal export path — streaming, format cap,
audit. The SQL is read again from the saved turn: the client sends only the step's
id, never a query.

post.description:
One turn of the flow editor's assistant. It changes the canvas the editor
sent and returns it in `done.definition` (null when nothing changed), with the
nodes it added or changed in `done.touched`: the editor applies it as one Undo
step. It never saves, runs or schedules the flow.

One turn of the script editor's assistant. Its proposal of files comes back in
`done.proposal` (null when it proposed nothing): the editor applies it if the person
wants. No data reaches the model: the code, the environment, the names of the
variables and of the inputs' columns, and the error of a failed run; in metadata-only
mode not even that (`done.error_withheld`: the person is told).

get.description:
The user's latest conversation with the flow editor's assistant about this
flow, to show again when the editor opens it; null when there is none.

post.description:
A copy of the flow in its folder, as «name (i)», under the same rules as a new
flow. The definition is copied as it is, Output nodes included: whoever made the
copy renames its outputs before running it. Schedule and failure alerts stay
with the original.

get.description:
Exports the flow as a dbt project (zip). `target=duckdb` (federation), `native`
(the origin warehouse, SQL translated through sqlglot) or `clickhouse` (the
customer's ClickHouse, which reads the Postgres/MySQL sources live). The gateway
resolves flow→operations and sources→DB tables, the engine compiles and zips.
Without options: the complete project with the default values (see POST).

post.description:
The dbt export with the download dialog's choices: target, complete project or
folder for an existing project, names, sources declared already, schema,
materializations, tests, email (see `DbtOptions`).

get.description:
What the download dialog needs: the possible targets (or why not, in the language of
whoever asks), the sources of each with the default name, the outputs with the
allowed materializations.

post.description:
"I have this flow open": the editor's heartbeat. It answers with who ELSE has it
open. It blocks and prevents nothing — it warns, because whoever saves last
overwrites the other. Whoever sees the flow sees who is looking at it too; nobody
else.

get.description: The flow's version history (the newest is the current one).

schema.title: Response List Flow Versions Flows  Flow Id  Versions Get

post.description:
Promotes an old version to current: its definition becomes the flow's and is
recorded as a new version at the head of the history.

get.description:
Run statistics from the flow's run history (kind flow/orchestration): how many,
successes/failures, last run, average time.

post.description:
Queues the flow's ORCHESTRATION (refresh/output/runflow nodes in the edges' order),
which an orchestrator runs with the user's authority. RUN on the project is needed;
the RBAC of the single steps (CONNECT of the refreshes, EDIT/CONNECT of the outputs)
is checked again during the orchestration.

It creates a tracing 'orchestration run' at once and returns its id: the frontend
polls it (`GET /runs/{id}`) until SUCCESS/FAILURE — so flows without an Output node
(which make no runs of their own) have an observable state too.

`mode`: "development" (default) uses the editor's engine; "production" uses the
flow's production engine — as the scheduler would — to try it by hand before
scheduling.

put.description:
Sets/disables the scheduled run (5-field cron; '' = off). RUN on the flow's project
is needed, and the flow must have at least one Output node (without, a scheduled run
would produce nothing). At fire time the gateway resolves the CURRENT definition
again and launches the Outputs with the authority of whoever schedules (EDIT/CONNECT
of the single outputs checked again then).

schema.title: Response List Runs Flows  Flow Id  Runs Get

post.description:
A dry run of the email node: makes the REAL attachment and sends it to WHOEVER ASKS,
to see what it looks like before sending it to someone else.

The server sets the recipient (`user.email`): the client cannot choose it, or this
route would be the handiest way around the allowed domains. The rest of the path is
the same as a normal run — the same RBAC (RUN on the flow, CONNECT on the
connection), the same audit — so the trial really checks what will happen, not an
imitation of it.

Publishing, destination and copy are dropped: a trial must not write anything
anywhere.

get.description:
The runs' activity for the calendar plot of the Flows page: counts by DAY (heatmap)
or, with `day`, by HOUR (drill-down). Each run is an event; the breakdown tells the

post.description:
A datasource from a database: EDIT on the destination folder + CONNECT on the
connection's folder (the barrier on the credentials). The first ingest starts at
once; the parquet is a snapshot, the refresh replaces it.

A datasource from Excel files on SharePoint (path, globs too, + sheet).

It is a `kind="database"` datasource in every respect — manual and scheduled refresh,
import history, spinner, snapshot swap — with `source_type="sharepoint"` and
`source_ref` = JSON {path, sheet, format, csv}: only WHO brings the data changes (see
launch_ingest_run).

Datasource from the files of a folder on an SFTP server (folder + glob).

A `kind="database"` datasource like the SharePoint one — manual and scheduled
refresh, import history, snapshot swap — with `source_type="sftp"` and
`source_ref` = JSON {folder, pattern, format, sheet, csv}: only WHO brings the
data changes (see launch_ingest_run). EDIT on the folder + CONNECT on the
connection's folder, as for every database datasource.

Datasource from the files of a folder of a bucket («S3 folder»): the bucket
(empty = the connection's default), a folder and a glob, with placeholders,
variables and the append mode as the SFTP datasource.

A `kind="database"` datasource — refresh, schedule, history, snapshot swap —
with `source_type="s3"` and the JSON of the folder in `source_ref`. EDIT on
the folder + CONNECT on the connection's folder, as for every database
datasource; the connection is the S3 one of the Output nodes.

Datasource from an HTTP API: the call (path, query, headers, body,
variables, pagination, the shape of the answer, the refresh mode) is made at
each refresh.

A `kind="database"` datasource like the SharePoint and SFTP ones — manual and
scheduled refresh, import history, snapshot swap — with `source_type="api"`
and `source_ref` = the call as JSON. The engine checks the call FIRST (the
placeholders, the variables, the JMESPath…): a call that cannot work is
refused before anything is saved. EDIT on the folder + CONNECT on the
connection's folder, as for every database datasource.

A datasource from one tab of a Google Sheets spreadsheet (and an optional range).

A `kind="database"` datasource like the SharePoint one — manual and scheduled
refresh, import history, snapshot swap — with `source_type="gsheets"` and
`source_ref` = JSON {spreadsheet_id, spreadsheet_name, sheet_id, sheet, range}:
only WHO brings the data changes (see launch_ingest_run). EDIT on the folder +
CONNECT on the connection's folder, as for every database datasource.

A copy of the datasource in its folder, as «name (i)»: its definition and its
data. The data file is copied on the storage to one of its own, since two
datasources sharing a file would lose it when either is refreshed or deleted.

A copy of a database datasource refreshes like the original, so it asks for
CONNECT on the connection's folder, as creating one does. The data contract
comes along, to be checked again; the refresh schedule, the contract's alerts
and the flow that published the original stay with the original.

Runs the source again and replaces the snapshot: RUN on the datasource's folder +
CONNECT on the connection's. One refresh at a time.

put.description:
Sets/disables the scheduled refresh (5-field cron). An empty `cron` = disable. RUN on
the datasource + CONNECT on the connection are needed: scheduling authorizes REPEATED
refreshes, so the same authority as the manual refresh. The scheduled refreshes will
run with the authority of WHOEVER sets the schedule (captured here in
`refresh_scheduled_by`).

delete.description:
Deletes the catalog item AND (deferred) the parquet blob.

A deliberate order: the catalog FIRST (detaching the runs that reference it), and in
the SAME transaction the blob is marked for DEFERRED deletion: a run/preview in
progress may have resolved its key already and be about to read it, so it is not
deleted at once (avoids the 404 while reading). The scheduler's sweep deletes it
after the grace. The flows referencing it will fail in preview with the standard
missing-source error — consistent with how datasets are deleted.

put.description:
Creates or replaces the contract, then checks it on the current data. The check here
cannot block anything (there is no new snapshot to refuse): it only says whether the
data there already respects it.

post.description:
A copy of the connection in its folder, as «name (i)», password included: it
stays encrypted as it is, and CONNECT on the folder is what lets anyone use it
in the first place.

Tests a connection BEFORE saving it (the UI's form), with only the secret written in
the form. For SFTP in two steps (see `test_connection`): it shows the
server's host key without sending credentials; with `expected_fingerprint` it
tests the credentials against exactly that key. It stores nothing.

Tests a saved connection. For SFTP this is trust on first use, in two steps,
and no credential ever goes to a key that is not accepted:

1. without `expected_fingerprint`: the engine reads the server's key; if it is
   not the accepted one (never accepted, or changed) it closes WITHOUT
   authenticating and the answer says `needs_acceptance`, with the key and the
   previous one. Nothing is stored. With the accepted key it tests the
   credentials as for any connection;
2. with `expected_fingerprint` (the key shown in step 1, which the user
   compared and accepts): the engine sends the credentials only if the server
   offers exactly that key. After a success the key is stored, with an audit
   line naming the previous one.

The files a folder + glob takes on this server: the feedback while the
datasource is being set up, BEFORE importing.

«Try the call» of the datasource dialog, BEFORE saving: the first page of the
first call with the connection's credentials — the request as sent (secrets
masked), the status, an excerpt of the answer and the first rows. CONNECT on
the connection's folder: it is a call made with its credentials.

The files (Excel, CSV) a path (globs too) takes on this site: the feedback while the
datasource is configured, BEFORE importing.

The spreadsheets shared with the service account (through the Drive API), to
choose one while the datasource is set up. Without the Drive API: a 400 saying so,
and the dialog takes the spreadsheet's link instead. CONNECT on the connection's
folder: it is a call made with its key.

A spreadsheet given by its link or id: its title and its tabs, and the tab the
link pointed at (`#gid=`), BEFORE the datasource is saved.

The first rows of a tab as the import will read them, with the types of the
columns: the header's problems show here, before the datasource exists.

The objects a folder + glob takes in the bucket (every expansion of its
placeholders, and the values without a file): «Check the files» of the «S3
folder» datasource, BEFORE importing. CONNECT on the connection's folder.

The live preview of the placeholders of a form (a datasource's folder and
glob, an Output's file name, folder, key or subject): each template's value
now, in its time zone, or the message of what is wrong — the engine's
checker, the same that validates at save time and before a run. Any signed-in
user: nothing is read, it is arithmetic on dates. A Pushmail cell's names of months
and days come in the language of whoever runs the group, the person asking.

get.description:
A table's columns and their types (a read of one row): the SQL script editor's
list and completion. CONNECT on the connection's folder.

The flow's lineage in the OpenLineage standard: a `JobEvent` with what it reads and
writes, rebuilt from the definition (without running). To download as a file or to
give to a collector.

Sends the flow's static lineage to the configured collector (to fill a catalog with

The lineage graph. Without `type`+`id` it returns the WHOLE graph over the readable
objects; with them, the subgraph centred within `depth` hops in the requested
direction (upstream / downstream / both).

Projects the active schedules (flows + datasource refreshes) over the next `days`
days and returns the day×hour grid of the load + the critical slots (collisions
beyond the workers' capacity).
Audit events, newest first, paginated and filterable.

get.description:
Sign-ins (logins) per hour in the last `hours` hours, successful vs failed. Bucketed
in the deployment's zone so the hour axis is in local time.

The open sessions, one per browser or script, newest first: the first `limit`, and
how many there are in all (on a public demo every guest sign-in is a row). They are
the rows that keep the tokens valid: closing one (DELETE) throws that browser out at
the next request.

delete.description:
Closes someone else's session (or one's own): its token stops holding at the next
request. Administrators only: the observer watches.

get.description:
The host's RAM in real time (used/available). Authentication is needed, but no
capability: it is a health indicator, not project data.

Without a node-exporter (MONITORING__NODE_EXPORTER_URL empty, as in a Kubernetes
installation that has none) the badge is off: 404 at once, without trying the call
nor writing a warning every time a browser asks.
Near-real-time overview: workers online, jobs running, jobs waiting.

post.description:
Stops (revoke + terminate) a job running on a worker, or removes it from the queue
when still waiting.

get.description:
The engines' catalog, with the installation's policy applied already.

It is NOT a blind forward, and it is the only point where the engine's catalog is
rewritten: the engine knows what is technically available, the gateway knows what
the administrator allows. A disabled engine comes back `available: false` with
`disabled_by_admin: true`, because the selector must be able to say WHY — «not
allowed here» is not «not configured», and showing them alike would send the user
looking for an environment variable that has nothing to do with it.

post.description:
Which nodes of a flow have their result in the step cache (the editor's
halo). The chains are the ones previews send, so they are checked like a
preview's: sources pinned to the engine's bucket and readable by the user.
The export for API callers: the file comes back in the response.

Upload (streaming towards the engine) + recording the ownership.

The engine's answer is a small JSON (IngestResult): it is buffered to record who owns
the dataset just created — the basis of the read check on uploads not inside a saved
flow yet.

EDIT somewhere is needed: the upload has no folder to ask the permission on, and
without this check a read-only account could write into the installation's bucket
(see permissions.can_upload).

get.description:
What runs now. `disabled_reason`: "kubernetes" off Kubernetes (Docker Compose),
"off" when the chart's clusterView is off; `error` when the API did not answer.

ActiveSession.title: ActiveSession
ActiveSession.description: An open session (a browser, a script) and whose it is.

ActivityBucket.title: ActivityBucket
ActivityBucket.description:
The counts of a bucket of the calendar plot: a day (key=YYYY-MM-DD) or an hour
(key='00'..'23'). Each run is an event; the breakdown tells the outcome
(successes/failures) and the origin (manual/scheduled) apart.

ApiCallSpec.title: ApiCallSpec
ApiCallSpec.description:
The call of an «API call» datasource: what it asks, how the answer becomes
rows, how it pages, and how a refresh lands (snapshot or append with keys).
The shape is checked here; the placeholders, the variables, the JMESPath and
the rest by the engine (`validate`) before anything is saved.

ApiDatasourceCreate.title: ApiDatasourceCreate
ApiDatasourceCreate.description: Datasource from an HTTP API: the call is made at each refresh.

ApiLimits.title: ApiLimits
ApiLimits.description: 0 = the deployment's limit (API__… on the engine); a value can only lower it.

ApiVariable.title: ApiVariable
ApiVariable.description:
A variable of a datasource (API call, SFTP, SharePoint, S3): a LIST —
`symbol = AAPL, MSFT`, one call or one expansion per value (every combination
of several) — or a RANGE — `day = today-7 .. today step 1d`, the values from
the start (included) to the end (excluded), with {day_end} the end of each
window. Checked by the engine (app.core.placeholders) before saving.

AppInfoOut.title: AppInfoOut
AppInfoOut.description:
Deployment info useful to the UI. `timezone` is the zone the schedules' cron
expressions are read in (see services/schedule.py).

Author.title: Author
Author.description: Whoever saved a version: the app reads with their rights.

BannerCreate.title: BannerCreate
BannerCreate.description: The level decides only the icon and the colour: a banner is always visible to all.

Capability.title: Capability
Capability.description:
What a subject may do on a project. Hierarchy (whoever may do more may do less):
VIEW < RUN < EDIT < MANAGE. CONNECT is orthogonal (using/creating data connections).
MANAGE includes everything.

CommentRequest.title: CommentRequest
CommentRequest.description:
Which comment, and what the screen shows beside it: the parameters' values and the clicks, as for
its numbers. What it reads and its instruction are the saved definition's. `moment`: `open` an opening, an
Apply, a refresh by hand; `refresh` an automatic refresh; `asked` a press of **Comment this view**.

ConnectionOut.title: ConnectionOut
ConnectionOut.description: The password NEVER leaves the API: only a flag saying whether it is set.

ConnectionTest.title: ConnectionTest
ConnectionTest.description:
A connection tested BEFORE it is saved (the form). It only uses the secret
typed in the form, never a stored one. SFTP: without `expected_fingerprint` the
test shows the server's host key and sends no credential; with it (the key the
user accepts), the credentials go only if the server offers exactly that key.

ContractSummary.title: ContractSummary
ContractSummary.description: A datasource's data contract state, for the listings.

DashboardRow.title: DashboardRow
DashboardRow.description: A row of the Dashboards tab: the dashboard, where it lives, who made it, who reads it.

DataRequest.title: DataRequest
DataRequest.description:
What to read: the parameters' values, as for a report; `tiles` only some (none: every
one); `page` a table's page by tile, from 0; `state` the on-screen view, as a report's
(a column sorted, groups toggled); `clicks` what is chosen on a tile, which filters the others
on its dataset: {"tile", "values", "on"}, a matrix's `on` being "columns", and never an expression
(services/dashboards.py). `refresh` reads the data again, at most every 10 seconds per dashboard
for everyone: past that, it answers with what is kept and when it was read, as any request does.

DatasourceRef.title: DatasourceRef
DatasourceRef.description: The datasource the script writes, once it exists, for whoever may read it.

DbDatasourceCreate.title: DbDatasourceCreate
DbDatasourceCreate.description: A datasource from a database: the source's definition + the first ingest.

DbtOptions.title: DbtOptions
DbtOptions.description:
The download dialog's choices (administrators only). Every free value ends up in a
YAML, SQL or Jinja file: strict forms, nothing to inject. The default values give
the same project as the download without options.

EnginePolicyOut.title: EnginePolicyOut
EnginePolicyOut.description:
The state of an engine for the installation.

`flows_using` is the migration's work list: disabling an engine does not stop the
flows that use it already, so the number says how many are still off standard —
otherwise the standardization would stay cosmetic.

FlowGroupCellLabel.title: FlowGroupCellLabel
FlowGroupCellLabel.description:
What the reader may know about a cell: its name and folder, or that the
object is gone, or that it sits in a folder the reader cannot see.

FlowGroupDefinition.title: FlowGroupDefinition
FlowGroupDefinition.description:
Rows are steps, run one after another; the cells of a row run in parallel.
None keeps an empty cell in its column, so the grid comes back as drawn.

FlowGroupRunOut.title: FlowGroupRunOut
FlowGroupRunOut.description:
A group run, with the state of every cell parallel to the group's grid:
{"state": waiting|running|succeeded|failed|skipped, "run_id", "error", "waited"}.

FlowOut.title: FlowOut
FlowOut.description: A list item: without `definition` (it can be heavy, only the editor needs it).

FlowScheduleUpdate.title: FlowScheduleUpdate
FlowScheduleUpdate.description:
Sets/disables the flow's scheduled run. An empty `cron` = off.
`production_engine`: omitted = unchanged; "" = back to the same as development.

FlowStatsOut.title: FlowStatsOut
FlowStatsOut.description: A flow's run statistics (from the run history).

FlowVersionOut.title: FlowVersionOut
FlowVersionOut.description: A version of a flow's definition (history + promotion).

GsheetsDatasourceCreate.title: GsheetsDatasourceCreate
GsheetsDatasourceCreate.description: A datasource from one tab of a Google Sheets spreadsheet, read at every refresh.

GsheetsTab.title: GsheetsTab
GsheetsTab.description:
One tab of a spreadsheet: its id (`gid` in the link: a renamed tab is still found
by it), its title when chosen, and an optional A1 range inside it.

GsheetsTabsQuery.title: GsheetsTabsQuery
GsheetsTabsQuery.description: The spreadsheet as the user pasted it: its link (from the browser) or its id.

HostKeyAcceptance.title: HostKeyAcceptance
HostKeyAcceptance.description:
SFTP: the key the user accepts — the one a previous test showed. A database: the
encryption of the form being edited (`extra`, only `tls` and `ca_cert` are taken), to
test it with the stored password before saving: same host, same account, so the secret
goes nowhere it did not go already.

ImageConfigOut.title: ImageConfigOut
ImageConfigOut.description: What an image does when nothing overrides it (container_registry.image_config).

InputInfo.title: InputInfo
InputInfo.description:
A declared input as this reader may know it: a datasource they cannot read, or
that no longer exists, keeps only its alias.

LocaleChange.title: LocaleChange
LocaleChange.description: The language chosen in the interface: one of its five.

MeOut.title: MeOut
MeOut.description:
Oneself. Beware: unlike `UserOut`, here `is_superuser` and `is_observer` are
EFFECTIVE — `routes/auth.py` computes them with `permissions.is_admin`/`is_observer`,
so they account for the groups. It is the field the frontend decides what to show
on, and it must answer «may I?», not «do I have the flag?».

MemoryOut.title: MemoryOut
MemoryOut.description:
The host's RAM. `available` is MemAvailable (not MemFree): it accounts for the
reclaimable cache/buffers, so it is the memory really allocatable.

ParametersRequest.title: ParametersRequest
ParametersRequest.description: The editor's definition, not saved yet, and the values chosen so far in its preview.

PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange
PasswordChange.description:
One's own password: the current one proves it is the owner at the keyboard,
not someone who found the session open.

PlaceholderPreviewQuery.title: PlaceholderPreviewQuery
PlaceholderPreviewQuery.description:
The live preview of templates in a form: each one's value now («today:
export_20261018.csv»), or what is wrong with it. `kind` input (a datasource's
folder/glob, with its variables) or output (an Output's file name, folder,
key or subject: `targets` says which).

ProblemOut.title: ProblemOut
ProblemOut.description:
A problem as the engine says it, and a refused save lists them: the item (its id,
none for the report, a dataset or a parameter), the property (`columns[0].value`,
`datasets[orders].source.sql`), the position in an expression (0 = its first
character) and how many characters.

PublishSpec.title: PublishSpec
PublishSpec.description: A request to publish the run's output as a named datasource.

PushmailAttachmentCell.title: PushmailAttachmentCell
PushmailAttachmentCell.description:
A datasource of a Pushmail cell: its file's name (a template with the Outputs'
placeholders, `.xlsx` added) and the rows it may hold at most.

PushmailCell.title: PushmailCell
PushmailCell.description:
A Pushmail cell's settings: an email through an SMTP connection, one .xlsx per
datasource and one file per report or dashboard (docs/pushmail.md).

PushmailDashboardCell.title: PushmailDashboardCell
PushmailDashboardCell.description:
A dashboard of a Pushmail cell (docs/specs/dashboards.md, «Going out»): rendered when the
cell runs, with the rights of whoever runs the group, as a PDF or an image, with these
parameters; its file's name a template with the Outputs' placeholders (the extension added).

PushmailReportCell.title: PushmailReportCell
PushmailReportCell.description:
A report of a Pushmail cell (docs/specs/reports.md, «Sending»): rendered when the
cell runs, with the rights of whoever runs the group, in its format and with these
parameters; its file's name a template with the Outputs' placeholders (the extension
added). `inBody`: its summary as HTML in the email's body too, under the cell's text
(one report per cell).

ReportRow.title: ReportRow
ReportRow.description: A row of the Reports tab: the report, where it lives, who made it, who reads it.

RunActivityOut.title: RunActivityOut
RunActivityOut.description:
The runs' activity for the calendar plot of the Flows page: buckets by DAY (heatmap)
or by HOUR (drill-down). The buckets are in the client's LOCAL time (passed via
tz_offset); from_key/to_key bound the window.

RunDestinationSpec.title: RunDestinationSpec
RunDestinationSpec.description:
The output's destination (the flow's Output node): a database table, an
object/dataset on S3 or a file on an SFTP server. The connection is referenced by
id, the credentials NEVER pass through the client.

RunEmailSpec.title: RunEmailSpec
RunEmailSpec.description:
Sending the output as an email attachment (an Output node with destType="email").

The recipients are free text in the flow's definition, so this is the only kind of
destination that can send data to an arbitrary address. Two consequences, both
applied by the gateway and not by the client: the recipients are validated against
the connection's allowed domains, and every send ends up in the audit.

`stop_on_failure` (on by default) stops the flow's SEQUENCE, not only fails the run:
the steps downstream of a notification often take it for done.

RunMirrorSpec.title: RunMirrorSpec
RunMirrorSpec.description:
A copy of the output to an external S3 storage, AS WELL AS the publishing as a
datasource (not instead of it: for that there is `RunDestinationSpec` with
type="s3", where the writing IS the result).

Written at the path of its key at every run: the same object overwritten, or —
when the key holds placeholders (`copia/{date}.parquet`) — one per day or per
run. No partitions. Best effort: a failed copy, or a key whose placeholders
cannot be resolved (then the copy is skipped), never fails the run nor the
publish; the outcome is recorded on the run.
The connection is referenced by id: the credentials do not pass through the client.

Parquet ONLY, and not by oversight: the format is not a choice because the file's
name and the format would be independent, and a CSV called `.parquet` would be
opened as parquet by whoever reads it downstream. Removing the choice makes the
mistake impossible instead of warning that it is possible.

RunProgress.title: RunProgress
RunProgress.description: Where a run not finished yet stands, for whoever looks at it.

RunSearchOut.title: RunSearchOut
RunSearchOut.description:
A run in the global run search: as RunOut + the names of the flow / the datasource
/ whoever started it, to show them without resolving them on the client.

S3DatasourceCreate.title: S3DatasourceCreate
S3DatasourceCreate.description:
Datasource from the files of a folder of a bucket («S3 folder»), through an
S3 connection: the bucket (empty = the connection's default), a folder (key
prefix) and a glob; the reading options of the SFTP datasource. All matching
objects are read at each refresh and stacked into one table.

SavedViewOut.title: SavedViewOut
SavedViewOut.description:
`datasource_name` is resolved on the server: a folder's listing must be able to say
WHAT the view is about without the client resolving N ids.

ScriptRunOut.title: ScriptRunOut
ScriptRunOut.description: A run of the script: its orchestration row, with what its script run says.

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description:
A resource found. `project_*` says WHERE it is: for a folder it is the folder that
contains it, for everything else the folder that hosts it — without it, a result
with a common name cannot be told from another.

SearchOut.title: SearchOut
SearchOut.description:
`counts` feeds the kind selector with the numbers: it is computed anyway to sort,
so it does not cost one more query.

SftpCsvOptions.title: SftpCsvOptions
SftpCsvOptions.description: How the CSV files of an SFTP folder are read (the options of the file sources).

SftpDatasourceCreate.title: SftpDatasourceCreate
SftpDatasourceCreate.description:
Datasource from the files of a folder on an SFTP server: a folder and a glob.
All matching files are read at each refresh and stacked into one table. Folder
and glob may hold placeholders and variables (FileTemplatesSpec).

SharePointDatasourceCreate.title: SharePointDatasourceCreate
SharePointDatasourceCreate.description:
A datasource from Excel and CSV files on SharePoint: a path (globs too), the format,
the sheet of the workbooks and the reading options of the CSV. Several matching
files are stacked into one table. The path may hold placeholders and variables
(FileTemplatesSpec).

SourceOption.title: SourceOption
SourceOption.description: A source (connection, schema) as the data team's project wants it.

SqlScriptRunOut.title: SqlScriptRunOut
